D13 conditions 1 and 3 had no mechanical check.
Lint allow-list was open-ended.
D13 did not name the as_of clock. Resolved by owner ruling R4.
D10 'no verdicts', Consequences 'expiry bands' and the D13 heading contradicted D13.
RSASSA-PSS hash parameter and EC group-order definition were missing.
R1 fetcher lacked alert, readiness and failure-behaviour obligations.
CaStore count method query cost unbounded.
A registered issuer with no CRL entry had no wording.
Owner rulings recorded only in the ADR.
Registration securable undefined under RBAC off.

Registered CA certificates were not barred as trust anchors; URL schemes and DNS rebinding unstated.
Delta, partitioned and hold CRLs and CA re-key were unhandled.
Serial and issuer matching had no canonical form.
Yuzu-CA 'security revocations' label is a verdict the free-text reasons do not support.
SSH counts could be narrowed by scope or confinement.
ISO-week series had no time zone, span or partial-week flag.
CH-5 required results to change only with the caller's T.
CRL staleness disclosure was a clock comparison outside D13 (also unhappy-path UP-2).
'Checked in CI' covered three allow-listed fields only (also UP-8).
Yuzu-CA widgets lacked twins, audit verb and 503-never-0 (also UP-9).
R1's operator-choice argument would admit any operator-configured feed.
Design doc offered Inventory/Security securables D12 rules out.
D5 reversal and Ratification disagreed on which ruling owns the D6 CaStore exception (also sg-8).
The ADR said the PR description records R1-R4; it did not.
A per-certificate 'revoked' could be stated from issuer and serial alone (planted or DN-colliding certificate).
Expired-certificate cause was ambiguous.
'Not listed' from a reason-partitioned CRL did not name the partition.
Extending the authz floor for a URL list fits none of its inclusion classes (also N-C).
Count wording said the agent verifies the signature; D5 requires server verification.
One table row credited R1 for the Yuzu-CA widgets.
